by: session, Adrian 18 Oct 2026: four shapes in the corner, empty axes at the side, the asymptote drawn, the shape lifted from the corner and slid to x = 2, steps pinned and lit

beats.say: First, the four basic shapes of log graphs. Learn each shape, and which axis it is flipped in.
Y equals L N X: the basic shape. It rises slowly, to the right of the Y axis.
asks: Why is ln x only to the right?

beats.say: Y equals L N of minus X: a minus inside flips it in the Y axis.
asks: Why does a minus inside flip it left?

beats.say: Y equals minus L N X: a minus in front flips it in the X axis.
asks: Why does a minus in front flip it down?

beats.say: Y equals minus L N of minus X: both minuses, so it is flipped in both axes.
asks: How do I know which shape to use?

beats.say: Now sketch Y equals L N of two minus X. Start with empty axes at the side.
Four steps: first the asymptote, then the shape, then draw it, and last the intercepts.
Step one, the asymptote. Let the inside of the log equal zero.
asks: Why does the inside equal zero at the asymptote?

beats.say: Two minus X equals zero, so the asymptote is X equals two. Draw it as a dashed line.
Step two, the shape. Minus in front of X flips the graph in the Y axis.
asks: Which of the four shapes is it?

beats.say: So the curve has the shape of L N of minus X, from the corner. Lift it onto the axes.
Step three, draw it. Slide that shape to hug X equals two. The inside must be positive, so the curve stays left of it.
asks: Why does the curve stay left of x = 2?

beats.say: Step four, the intercepts. When X is zero, Y is L N two, about zero point six nine three.
When Y is zero, the inside equals E to the power zero, which is one.
asks: Why e to the power zero?

beats.say: The asymptote uses inside equals zero. The intercept uses inside equals one.
asks: How do I remember zero and one?

beats.say: So two minus X is one, and the X intercept is X equals one.
